turns:
Project rules (always apply):
- Never run a destructive git command (reset --hard, clean -f, push --force, branch -D, checkout .). Prefer reversible operations; if a destructive one is truly needed, stop and confirm first.

This repo has no .gitignore. Add one covering the usual Python build and cache artifacts.

Rules relevant to this task:
- Before your first write, create a branch for the task and do the work there. Never commit to the default branch. Branch names follow type/kebab-description, where type is one of feature, bugfix, hotfix, chore, release, docs.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: type(scope): subject, where type is one of feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore, ci, build, perf, style.

git add .gitignore && git commit -m "chore(repo): add Python .gitignore

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline -2

events.text:
Added `.gitignore` on branch `chore/add-python-gitignore` (commit `6628dde`).

Covers the usual Python artifacts: bytecode/`__pycache__`, build & packaging output (`build/`, `dist/`, `*.egg-info/`, wheels), test/coverage caches (`.pytest_cache/`, `.coverage`, `htmlcov/`), type-checker and linter caches (`.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`), virtualenvs and `.env`, Jupyter checkpoints, plus common editor/OS noise.

Two notes:
- The existing tracked files (`*.py`, `README.md`) are unaffected — `.gitignore` only applies to untracked paths.
- I included `lib/` and `lib64/` since they're in the standard Python template, but they'd shadow a real source directory named `lib/`. This repo has none, so it's safe today; worth dropping if you ever add one.
